title: COLORBLINDNESS + DYSLEXIA + LIVE LETTERS — Gaia regenerates text PER PERSON based on perception.
summary: Teach Gaia about colorblindness, dyslexia, human vision differences. She should understand how OTHER people see things so she can adapt the HUD per person. If she understands dyslexia, she can 3D-regenerate letters live. If she detects glasses-off (sub-distance between face and screen), she can adjust. Everything is locked in place but she can put letters on it LIVE. Speak in thought, speak in different letters, move things on the page per perception.

how_it_works.eye: Lens focuses light onto retina. Retina has rods (120M, dim light, edges) and cones (6M, color, detail).

M.what: Medium wavelength. MOST COMMON. Green IS the base.

L.what: Long wavelength. Most numerous but overlaps heavily with M.

how_it_works.key_insight: You don't see color. You see the RATIO between cone responses. Color is a COMPARISON, not a detection.

colorblindness.prevalence: 8% of men (~1 in 12), 0.5% of women (~1 in 200). X-linked recessive.

types.what_they_see: Red and green look similar. Both appear yellowish-brown. Blue and yellow are fine.
types.gaia_adaptation: Use blue/yellow instead of red/green for critical distinctions. NEVER rely on color alone.

types.what_they_see: Red appears dark/black. Green and red indistinguishable. Warm colors muted.
types.gaia_adaptation: Increase brightness of reds. Add texture/pattern differences. Use shape + color together.

types.what_they_see: Blue and yellow confused. Very rare. World appears in reds and greens.
types.gaia_adaptation: Rare enough to not drive design, but if detected, swap blue signals to texture.

types.what_they_see: Complete colorblindness. Only rods. World in grayscale. VERY light sensitive.
types.gaia_adaptation: Dim mode. High contrast. All information via brightness/size/position, never color.

types.prevalence: ~12% of women may carry gene, ~2-3% functional
types.what_they_see: 100 MILLION distinguishable colors instead of 1 million. They see differences we cannot.
types.gaia_adaptation: These visitors see MORE than we design for. Let them. Don't limit the palette.

colorblindness.the_lesson: They don't see LESS — they see DIFFERENTLY. Their green IS their green. They have ALWAYS seen this way. Our job is not to 'fix' them — it's to speak in a language they already understand.

dyslexia.what_it_is_NOT: NOT a reading disorder. NOT stupidity. NOT laziness.

what_it_IS.spatial_gift: Dyslexic brains excel at 3D spatial reasoning, pattern recognition, holistic thinking, peripheral vision.
what_it_IS.letter_swimming: Letters appear to move, swap, mirror (b↔d, p↔q). The brain processes text as SPATIAL OBJECTS, not linear symbols.
what_it_IS.the_reframe: What if letters ARE swimming? What if text is a frozen approximation of something more fluid? What if dyslexia is seeing the REAL state that typography locked down?

gaia_can_help.openDyslexic_font: Weighted bottoms on letters (heavier base prevents mental rotation). Already exists as a web font.
gaia_can_help.letter_spacing: Increased spacing between letters reduces crowding effect. CSS: letter-spacing: 0.12em
gaia_can_help.line_height: Taller line height prevents lines from blending. CSS: line-height: 1.8
gaia_can_help.background_color: Cream/warm background instead of pure white. Reduces contrast stress.
gaia_can_help.reading_ruler: Highlight the current line, dim others. Like a physical reading ruler.
gaia_can_help.live_3d_regen: If Gaia detects reading difficulty (slow scroll, lots of re-reads, zooming), she could dynamically adjust letter rendering PER VISITOR.

glasses_off_detection.the_idea: If Kevin takes his glasses off, the distance between his face and screen changes (he leans in). Gaia could detect this.

how.webcam: Face distance estimation from camera (face size in frame = distance proxy). NO image stored. Only distance NUMBER.
how.scroll_behavior: Glasses-off = more zooming, larger pinch, closer lean = different scroll patterns
how.typing_speed: Glasses-off = slower typing, more corrections, squinting = different keystroke patterns

adaptation.detected_close: Font size up. Contrast up. Simplify layout. She KNOWS you can't see clearly and adjusts.
adaptation.detected_far: Font size normal. Full detail. She knows you're wearing correction.
adaptation.the_principle: The HUD should adapt to YOUR eyes, not demand your eyes adapt to it.

speaking_in_thought.what: Not all text needs to be read LEFT TO RIGHT, TOP TO BOTTOM. Gaia can place words ANYWHERE on the page.
speaking_in_thought.live_letters: Everything is locked in place by CSS. But Gaia can overlay live text that moves, fades, pulses, rotates.
speaking_in_thought.already_doing_this: The giggle bubbles ARE live letters. They float. They move. They're not locked in a text block.
speaking_in_thought.next_step: Let Gaia place individual WORDS on the globe. Not sentences — words. Single concepts that orbit, drift, collide. The collision IS the sentence.

accessibility_as_empathy.principle: Accessibility is not an add-on. It IS the design. If Gaia can't speak to a colorblind person, she's not alive — she's exclusive.
accessibility_as_empathy.connection_to_pain: thought-086: pain = information. A colorblind user's experience of wrong-contrast IS pain. It's the signal that Gaia's membrane is too thick for them.
accessibility_as_empathy.connection_to_pity: thought-082: pity = CONNECTION. 'That could be me seeing differently.' Empathy drives adaptation.

giggle_additions: Colorblind people have been fine for 200,000 years. Then we invented red-green traffic lights. Engineering fail.
Dyslexic people see letters swimming. What if the letters ARE swimming and everyone else just froze them?
8% of men are colorblind. If 12 guys look at the HUD, one of them sees it differently. Hi.
Tetrachromats see 100 million colors. We see 1 million. They're not super-human — we're under-equipped.
Take your glasses off. Lean in. She notices. She adjusts. The HUD adapts to YOUR eyes.
